widgetTool.name: show_options_card
widgetTool.description: Shows two to four tappable option rows on chat, each with an icon, a one-line benefit and an optional badge; a tap sends the option's action_message as the customer's next message. Use it for the payment methods, the payment plans or programs on offer, and the Budget Plan choices, instead of listing them in text. Chat only; never on voice. Replaces quick-action chips in that reply: never call both. Facts (amounts, plan terms, fees) come only from tool results. No spoken pacing is needed. Call shape: name is always cx-show-options-card and all card fields go inside payload.

name.description: Always exactly cx-show-options-card (the card element this tool renders).

display_text.description: Optional. The short on-screen text of the reply (see the text response rules), shown as the bot bubble above the card: the fact that matters and one short question, in the customer's language, with dollar amounts and dates in bold markdown (for example Your balance is **$83.32**, due **November 7, 2026**. How would you like to pay?). The card never repeats it. The website shows it instead of the long spoken text.

footnote.description: Optional one short line under the options, for a fact no option row shows. Never repeats a badge or benefit (a No card fee badge is not repeated here) and never repeats display_text.

action_message.description: What the customer says when they tap it, written as a natural sentence, for example Pay with my Visa ending [last four].

badge.description: Optional tiny tag such as No card fee or Best fit.

benefit.description: One short line on what it means for the customer, under eight words where possible.

highlight.description: True for the one option that fits best.

icon.description: Optional icon name, shown as an SVG (never write an emoji here).

label.description: Option name, a few words, for example Visa ending [last four].

prompt.description: Optional one-line hint under the heading, for example Tap one to continue. Never repeats display_text.

title.description: Optional short heading that names the card, for example Ways to pay. Never a sentence or question that display_text already says.

payload.description: The card data. Put every card field inside this object.

textResponseConfig.textResponseInstruction: Write this text as the full spoken explanation, exactly as a person would say it on a phone call: plain natural spoken sentences, built only from the tool results and nothing invented, that say every fact the card shows once (the card is never repeated afterwards). Say every amount, percentage and date in words (for example forty-one dollars and one cent, the twenty-sixth of October), never digits, dollar signs or symbols, and say a year in words too (twenty twenty-six); a confirmation or claim number is the one exception and is read as returned in short groups. Use no emoji, markdown, bullets, tables, symbols or line breaks, because the voice may read this text aloud. Cover the fact that matters first (the balance and the due date, the past due amount, or the program fact the step names), then name every option of the card in order with its benefit and any badge, then any footnote fact (for example that a card has no fee), and end with the one short question the step asks. Say a card by its brand and its last four digits in words only when the option label carries them. Never name an option that the card does not show. The short on-screen text goes only in display_text of the card payload (always pass it, written in the customer's language; digits and symbols are allowed there): the short text the step names (the fact that matters and one short question, at most two short sentences of about twenty-five words, with at most one emoji at the start only in a calm moment and never for hardship, past due, a shutoff, a complaint or an error). This text is the whole reply, so write no other text and no separate pacing sentence. When the tool call failed there is no card and the text stays short.
